title: Hong Kong's 24/7 FITNESS says unauthorized access to its member system exposed some members' data, Wen Wei Po reports
date_note: Wen Wei Po says the company found the unauthorized access on 20 November.
geo_basis: The page names Hong Kong as the setting; no city or address for the company
summary: Wen Wei Po reports that 24/7 FITNESS found unauthorized access to its member system on 20 November. Data of some current and former members was exposed, including contact details, photos, some ID card numbers and health declaration information. The Privacy Commissioner's Office received a breach notification on 21 November; the number affected is still being determined.
plain: A Hong Kong gym chain says someone accessed its member system without permission, exposing some members' contact details, photos, some ID card numbers and health declarations. How many people were affected is still being checked.
exec: A member system was accessed without authorization, exposing some current and former members' data, including some ID card numbers and health declarations; the affected number is still being determined.
action: The Privacy Commissioner advises, per Wen Wei Po, that organisations enable multi-factor authentication and access controls, run security assessments and penetration tests, and supervise vendors.

validation.note: Only Wen Wei Po was read; the company's own notice and the PCPD page were not read.

review.note: Compared title, date 20 Nov, PCPD 21 Nov, data items, advice against Wen Wei Po
